context_requirements: Expression of bile acid receptors (FXR/NR1H4, TGR5/GPBAR1, VDR, PXR) or bile acid transporters (NTCP/SLC10A1, ASBT/SLC10A2, OATP family)
Hepatic or intestinal lineage for robust FXR/TGR5-dependent transcriptional responses
Intact cholesterol synthesis machinery for feedback regulation
Capacity to mount oxidative stress and ER stress responses
falsifiers: No change in FOS, JUN, EGR1, or other immediate-early genes at 6 h in any line
No induction of oxidative stress or ER stress genes (HMOX1, DDIT4, TRIB3, CHAC1) at 6 or 24 h
No suppression of cholesterol synthesis genes (HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1) at 6 or 24 h
No antiproliferative or apoptosis signature at 24 h in any line
Responses are equally strong in all nine lines regardless of lineage, suggesting non-specific toxicity rather than bile acid receptor-mediated effects

evidence.supports: Bile acids activate nuclear receptors and GPCR signaling to regulate lipid, glucose, and energy homeostasis; toxic bile acids cause inflammation, apoptosis, and cell death.
Bile acids regulate metabolism and inflammation via FXR and TGR5 in enterohepatic and peripheral tissues.
Bile acid signaling is altered in NAFLD, with changes in FXR agonistic/antagonistic bile acids and hepatic gene expression.
Bile acids modulate intestinal FXR-FGF15 signaling, hepatic bile acid synthesis, and cholesterol/lipid metabolism.
Hydrophobic bile acids cause oxidative stress, ER stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis in hepatocytes and other cell types.

changes: Removed DNAJB1 and HSPA1A from proximal_up: generic heat-shock/proteostasis genes, not proximal bile-acid receptor targets.
Removed IER3 from proximal_up: generic immediate-early stress gene without bile-acid-specific support.
Kept HMOX1, DDIT4, TRIB3, CHAC1, SQSTM1 as they are supported by bile-acid oxidative/ER stress evidence (PMID 19360911).
Kept cholesterol synthesis genes (HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, EBP, NSDHL, INSIG1) in proximal_down as FXR-mediated feedback is supported (PMID 31672964).
Kept NR1H2 in proximal_down as a nuclear receptor feedback component, though evidence is indirect.
Kept late_up inflammatory/NF-kB genes (NFKB2, RELB, TICAM1, ICAM1, CXCL2, MMP1, MMP2, SPP1, SERPINE1) as bile-acid inflammation is supported (PMID 23897684, 28214524).
Kept late_down proliferation genes as antiproliferative/apoptotic bile-acid effects are supported (PMID 19360911).
Line responses retained: HEPG2 strong (hepatic, FXR-expressing), HT29/HCC515 moderate (intestinal/hepatic lineage), others weak due to lack of bile-acid receptor/transporter expression.
Kinetics and magnitude retained: fast immediate-early response with moderate 6 h and strong 24 h effects is consistent with bile-acid stress signaling.
Evidence list retained: all five abstracts support the stated claims about bile-acid signaling, metabolism, and toxicity.
